sequence.name: Thunderdome
sequence.text:
1
Thunderdome
1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Thunderdomes are advanced workouts for those who have plateaued. Beginners can make good progress with other workouts before attempting a Thunderdome.

For each stimulus in the section*, write or speak out each and every one of the following outputs, according to the stimulus type, without looking at the question stem or answer choices:

On an Argument, write or speak your own:

Weaken correct answer

Strengthen correct answer

Necessary assumption

Sufficient assumption

Method correct answer

Argument parts identifications

Parallel Skeleton

Parallel correct answer

Use your favorite topic as a consistent analogous base

This means all your Parallel correct answers can be about dogs or cars across all the questions in the section.

On a Debate, write or speak your own:

Controversy

Agreement

Loophole in both speakers

On a Paradox, write or speak your own:

Resolution

Inference

Contradiction

On a Premise Set, write or speak your own:

Three Inferences

Contradiction

sequence.name: Party Tricking Jail
sequence.text:
4
Party Tricking Jail
1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Party Tricking Jail is an advanced workout for those who want to push themselves to become true answer choice experts. Beginners can make good progress with other workouts before entering Party Tricking Jail.

Party Trick every question in an LR or RC section*.

This means you will only read the question stem and answer choices on each question before you select an answer on that question.

Do not look at the stimulus or passage.

Camo the section immediately after completing it.

The Camo will display all the questions that are wrong plus an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Do not look at the stimulus when you Camo.

Party Trick the returned questions again. Doubt your answers on the questions Camo displays and try to correct your answer.

Get as close to -0 on the Camo as you can.

OPTIONAL: Do not exit Party Tricking Jail until you reach -5 or better pre-Camo.

You can customize this accuracy goal to your personal needs.
SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Scavenger Hunt
sequence.text:
5
Scavenger Hunt
Instructions

At the end of the week, have a friend grade all your sections.

Ask your friend to only tell you how many you got wrong in each section.

This means your friend will only tell you that a given section was a -5. They will not tell you anything else about the section.

Go back to each section to find every wrong answer.

The goal is to correct every section to a -0 without using the answer key. 

Send your new answers to your friend to see how much you've improved.

Optional: Repeat this cycle until you get to -0 on each section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Hit List
sequence.text:
6
Hit List
Instructions

Make a spreadsheet with three columns, or use this template:

Column 1: Top 15 Question

Column 2: How This Question Works

Column 3: What I Can Take From This Question

Keep a list of the 15 hardest questions you've ever completed in your prep.

Each day, study two questions from the Hit List.

Dissect exactly how each question is working.

How does the question both camouflage and justify the correct answer?

What makes this question hard?

Figure out what you can take from this question.

And what can you work on in your process to improve your performance on questions that are difficult for the same reason going forward?

Continually add questions to and remove questions from your Hit List as some questions no longer feel difficult and others feel more challenging.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

This Routine forces you to look at the section from so many different perspectives all within one intense Routine.

It mixes in stimulus-only practice, answer-choice-only practice, test-day timed practice, and deep review – this refines your process, even when you're already scoring at a high level.

How This Should Be Done

If you need to cap your Thunderdome at 1 hour to complete this Routine within the amount of time you have that's fine. But the deeper you go, the more you'll get out of it.

The Test-Day Timed Sections should cut off when time is called, so they will take up the minority of your time in this Routine, but moving into Party Tricking directly afterwards offers a unique benefit.

Party Tricking is intuition-training and will provide a different perspective on the intuition-based approach that you just utilized in your test-day timed sections.

How to Move On

You can intersperse this Routine with PTs in the last month before your exam.

There's no pressing reason to move on from this Routine since it will always provide a valuable challenge.
